# The eBilling Company

> The eBilling Company builds The eBilling System, a matter-first enterprise
> legal management (ELM) and legal e-billing platform for in-house legal
> departments, with a collaboration portal for outside counsel.

## Positioning

The platform connects the legal operating lifecycle from business request and
matter creation through outside counsel collaboration, invoice review, budgets,
accruals, AP handoff, payment status, reconciliation, and reporting. It is
broader than a spend-only point tool because the matter remains the shared
system of record for both work and financial activity.

## Platform areas

- Intake and matter management: configurable requests, governed fields and
  managed lists, pending phase, required closure details, people, tasks, files,
  favorites, recents, and matter access controls.
- Outside counsel collaboration: firm and office billing records, separate
  portal identities, client grants, matter updates, timekeepers, rate requests,
  budgets, accruals, invoice submission, and post-matter firm scorecards.
- Legal e-billing: LEDES, PDF, and manual intake; duplicate and guideline
  validation; line adjustments; threshold-based escalation; shadow and credit
  invoice types; and correction history.
- Budgets and accruals: matter and phase planning, alternative fee arrangements,
  practice-group and entity rollups, fiscal calendars, burn views, firm proposals,
  accrual collection, and close controls.
- Finance loop: purchase-order requests and decision callbacks, invoice-to-PO
  balances, allocations, AP batches, per-system office billing identities,
  payment reconciliation, and managed currency rates.
- Reporting: a self-service cross-object builder with live previews, charts,
  text-to-report assistance, private/role/workspace sharing, scheduled email,
  and Excel/CSV/PDF exports; modular dashboards and cited review flags.
- Documents: Word templates with merge tags and test merges, record-side
  generation, PDF conversion, and iManage/NetDocuments/SharePoint adapters.
  External DMS connections require validation against the customer's tenant.
- Administration: six-entity CSV import with mapping, validation and error
  files; cascading lists; email rules and delivery logs; login announcements;
  user profiles, preferences, and delegation.

General-purpose Donna voice/chat, passkey enrollment, and standalone internal
time-entry capture are roadmap items, not represented here as shipped features.
Deployment and external integration requirements are agreed during evaluation.

## Product evaluation

Prospective customers can request access to a sandbox populated with synthetic
matters, firms, invoices, budgets, accruals, and reports. The sandbox supports
hands-on product evaluation without customer-data migration, production-system
connections, or a full implementation project. It must not be used for
privileged, confidential, personal, or production data.

## Security statements

- Tenant, matter, and firm access boundaries are enforced with PostgreSQL
  row-level security in addition to application authorization.
- In-house and outside counsel users operate in distinct identity contexts.
- Material workflow and financial events retain append-only audit history.
- AI may assist review and report composition, but professional decisions and
  deterministic monetary calculations remain outside the model.
- The company does not currently represent the product as SOC 2 certified.
  Certification claims will be published only when earned.
